case.fiction: The Abyss Legend (ABYSS LEGEND) in the game is a fictional machine. It only follows the structure of the case below and does not copy any real product or its graphics.
case.intro: In 2006 in Korea, there was an incident involving adult amusement arcades known as Bada Iyagi. Only confirmed facts are written here, with their sources.
case.me.after: After the omen, during the stretch in which the bonus was released, you played {rounds} rounds and wagered {bet} credits. The average bet per round was {avgAfter} in this stretch and {avgOther} in the other stretches. There were {otherRounds} rounds in the other stretches.
case.me.controls: While the bonus was running, you pressed STOP {stop} times, TURBO {turbo} times, AUTO {auto} times, and changed your bet {bets} times. Their effect on the result was zero.

case.me.omens: The omen appeared {n} times. At each of those moments the bonus amount had already been decided, and the total was {fixed} credits.
case.me.stayed: Staying at the seat did not change that amount. Even if you had left, you would have received the same amount. The {bet} credits you wagered after the omen were not for earning the bonus; they were new money wagered. This machine's return rate is {ret}, so the expected loss is about {loss} credits.
case.me.title: Linking with my session
case.p1: In April 2005, the Korea Media Rating Board passed Bada Iyagi in its rating review.
case.p2: By August 2006, adult amusement arcades such as Bada Iyagi, Hwanggeumseong and Screen Horse Racing had grown to 15,618, and the government launched a large-scale crackdown.
case.p3: This machine could pay up to 2.5 million won, 125 times the legal maximum prize of 20,000 won. A memory chain function, which accumulated points so that vouchers poured out in succession, was added illegally.
case.p4: During play the screen suddenly darkened while announcing a big win, and people were held in front of the machine. After symbols such as the clam (daehap) or animals such as whales and sharks appeared, wins continued in succession.
case.p5: Prize vouchers were originally meant for buying cultural goods, but they were exchanged for cash and in practice served as gambling chips. Circulation in August 2006 alone was about 2.7685 trillion won. According to industry analysis, circulation in the year before the incident was at least 30 trillion won.
case.p6: The Prime Minister formally apologized for the policy failure. The representatives of the manufacturer and the distributor were each sentenced to one year and six months in prison for illegal modification.
